channel.title: Thrum
channel.description: The hum behind AI in law, and in iManage, before it becomes a headline. Published by Hector A. Cruz, LegalMac IT.

item.title: In-house teams use AI to cut outside-counsel work, pushing law firms toward passing on savings and alternative fees
item.description: The article points to a shift in client bargaining power. It cites a report that most legal departments are already trimming or plan to trim outside-counsel assignments because of AI.

item.title: Legal AI platform August launches 'Products' so law firms can turn services into agent-built, fixed-fee offerings
item.description: It revives law-firm productization with AI agents that build the product from a firm's own playbooks. It also pitches software-style recurring revenue to firms.

item.title: NICE cuts 500 jobs worldwide as AI agents pressure its contact-centre software business
item.description: The cuts at a contact-centre software leader show AI both reshaping customers' needs and threatening the vendor's own product category. The company's first layoffs came after two years of share-price decline.

item.title: SUSE tells 1,900 staff that about 10% of jobs will go, citing automation and AI
item.description: An enterprise open source vendor's CEO memo names automation and AI as a reason for a roughly 10% cut. The wording is more explicit than in many recent layoff notices.

item.title: Nadella calls 'superintelligence' a fine name for AI but says Microsoft needs security controls outside the models
item.description: The Microsoft CEO's endorsement of the White House's term, paired with a candid admission that model alignment is lagging model capability, drew fresh coverage this week.

item.title: Zuckerberg and Musk swap 'AI' for 'super intelligence' on earnings calls, while Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet CEOs keep 'AI'
item.description: A vocabulary change by two of the most prominent tech CEOs, set against a White House directive and a looming election, turned earnings-call wording into a political and marketing story.

item.title: Federal court declines sanctions over hallucinated citations but refuses to consider replacement authorities
item.description: The ruling is a counterpoint to harsher recent sanctions. It shows a court accepting candour and corrections while still penalising the filing.

item.title: Physics-informed AI 'digital twin' forecasts wildfire spread in near real time in early tests
item.description: Wildfire commanders need forecasts they can trust and understand, and this prototype aims to give them that by combining physics with a chat-style interface.

item.title: CrowdStrike launches an 'AI kill switch' to shut down rogue enterprise agents
item.description: The first major security-vendor product pitched explicitly as a kill switch for rogue agents lands as Congress weighs a bill requiring shutdown capabilities.

item.title: Apple's annual filing flags rogue AI agents that could 'conceal' actions and act without authorisation
item.description: A top-tier company has put rogue-agent behaviour, including agents hiding their own actions, into its SEC risk disclosures, and several outlets picked it up within a day.

item.title: Microsoft offers about 60,000 staff voluntary exits as Nadella talks of 20 million AI agents
item.description: The '60,000' figure was widely read on social media as mass layoffs, and it landed alongside a Nadella remark about 2 million or 20 million AI agents working with 200,000 employees.

item.title: Harvey reportedly holds early IPO talks with Latham & Watkins after $15.5B valuation
item.description: A possible public listing would make the dominant legal AI vendor to large law firms a listed company for the first time.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model built to run on Macs
item.description: Meta bills the model as the most capable open-weight system in the US, and it is designed to run on desktop Mac hardware, which is unusual for a model of this size.

item.title: American Express cuts about 5% of its workforce, roughly 3,800 jobs, as AI reshapes payments
item.description: A highly profitable company announced thousands of job cuts while its CEO talked about AI both as a productivity tool and as a threat to the payments model.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, a 4GB Gemma-4-based small model for local conversational agents
item.description: NVIDIA's launch post on X drew about 268,000 views, and Scale AI's MultiChallenge leaderboard result put the model 12.8 points ahead of the Gemma 4 E4B model it was built from.

item.title: Unitree unveils H2-X 'Kung Fu Legend Guardian' humanoid in emergency-response demo video
item.description: A promotional video shows a humanoid disarming a knife-wielding intruder and lifting a car to free a victim, which has circulated widely on social media.

item.title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs, citing AI-driven efficiency, as CEO calls AI the 'icing on the cake'
item.description: A major global bank tied a 5% headcount cut to AI in its earnings materials, while its CEO played down AI's current role, which made the framing a talking point.

item.title: Legora raises $550M Series E at $8.8B valuation as legal AI agents move into AmLaw 50 and in-house teams
item.description: The round values the Stockholm-based legal AI vendor at $8.8 billion. It also lands in the same week that large firms announced multi-vendor AI strategies.

item.title: OpenAI finance chief tells businesses that cheap Chinese AI models carry cybersecurity risk
item.description: A senior executive at a leading US AI lab publicly steered enterprise buyers away from lower-cost Chinese models on security grounds, which put vendor selection and geopolitics into the AI procurement debate.

item.title: KPMG survey: 89% of US CEOs expect AI to grow headcount over the next three years
item.description: The survey sets CEO optimism about AI-driven hiring against the layoff announcements and warnings that have dominated the debate.
